title: Households are turning home into a resilience buffer, but security, comfort, and control remain need–experience gaps
source_unit: IKEA Life at Home Report 2026, based on YouGov, Crowd DNA, and GlobeScan research
geography: Global; quantitative life-at-home survey in 31 countries, with qualitative ethnographies in India, Spain, and the United States

observations.period: 2025 fieldwork reported in 2026; home needs and experienced gaps

denominator.unit: adults aged 18+ interviewed across 31 countries in the quantitative Life at Home study

security_important.unit: percent saying security at home is important

security_experienced_regularly.unit: percent experiencing security at home regularly

comfort_important.unit: percent saying comfort at home is important

comfort_experienced_regularly.unit: percent experiencing comfort at home regularly

control_important.unit: percent saying control at home is important

control_experienced_regularly.unit: percent experiencing control at home regularly

home_optimism.value: 65% of people happy with life at home are positive about the future versus 48% global average

observations.method: IKEA Life at Home quantitative online survey conducted by YouGov in 2025; each country weighted equally in global results and country samples weighted by gender, age and geography according to the source description.
observations.uncertainty: The need–experience gaps are descriptive and the home-optimism relationship is associational; the source does not establish that home conditions cause optimism, security, comfort or control, and the global result is not a household-income or housing-quality measure.
observations.subgroup: Adults aged 18+ in 31 countries, with life-stage and age contrasts reported by the source; country estimates and household circumstances remain distinct.
observations.counterinterpretation: People may report a better home experience because they are more optimistic, secure or resourced; the same home can provide emotional control while financial, housing, climate or political pressures remain unresolved outside it.

observations.period: 2025 fieldwork reported in 2026; household concerns, climate exposure, and consumer action

denominator.unit: adults aged 18+ interviewed across 31 countries in the quantitative Life at Home study

household_finance_concern.unit: percent identifying household finances and disposable income among top life-at-home concerns

physical_health_concern.unit: percent identifying physical health among top life-at-home concerns

economy_concern.unit: percent identifying the state of the economy among top life-at-home concerns

climate_personally_impacted.unit: percent feeling personally impacted by climate change

climate_action_taken.unit: percent reporting that they are already taking climate action

climate_action_motivated_by_saving.unit: percent saying saving money would motivate more climate action

climate_action_motivated_by_health.unit: percent saying health benefits would motivate more climate action

observations.method: IKEA Life at Home and people-and-planet consumer-insights materials; climate-action measures combine the report's quantitative survey evidence and should not be interpreted as verified emissions or household technology adoption.
observations.uncertainty: Concern, personal impact, reported action and motivation are different constructs; the data do not identify the specific action, cost, frequency, emissions effect, or whether action is sustained.
observations.subgroup: Adults across the 31-country quantitative frame, with age and life-stage differences in concerns; online access and country weighting boundaries apply.
observations.counterinterpretation: Climate action can be low-cost or symbolic, while financial pressure can limit expensive adaptation; saving money may motivate action without indicating climate-first values or durable consumption change.

observations.period: 2025 fieldwork reported in 2026; generational differences in home-life concerns

denominator.unit: adults aged 18+ interviewed across 31 countries; age comparisons reported for Gen Z ages 18–29 and Baby Boomers ages 61–79

gen_z_mental_health_concern.unit: percent of Gen Z respondents identifying mental health as a life-at-home concern

boomers_physical_health_concern.unit: percent of Baby Boomer respondents identifying physical health as a life-at-home concern

gen_z_screen_time_concern.unit: percent of Gen Z respondents identifying screen time as a life-at-home concern

boomers_societal_division_concern.unit: percent of Baby Boomer respondents identifying societal division as a life-at-home concern

life_stage_mechanism.value: the meaning of a resilient home varies by life stage: younger adults emphasize mental health and screen time while older adults emphasize physical health, economy and societal division

observations.method: IKEA report comparison of selected Gen Z and Baby Boomer concern items within the 2025 quantitative life-at-home survey.
observations.uncertainty: The source excerpt reports selected percentages rather than a full age-stratified table, and age differences are descriptive rather than causal; generational categories contain heterogeneous countries, incomes, housing conditions and life events.
observations.subgroup: Gen Z adults aged 18–29 and Baby Boomers aged 61–79 in the reported 31-country survey frame.
observations.counterinterpretation: Age differences may reflect life stage, cohort, health, housing, country composition or question salience rather than stable generational values; the report does not establish different household behavior or purchasing patterns.

related_sources.claim: Ingka Group report index and Life at Home research context.

boundary: This record adds consumer-perception evidence about home as a resilience, comfort, control, security and climate-action setting. It is a commercially commissioned online survey and qualitative research programme, not objective housing, income, welfare, emissions, mental-health, or longitudinal behavioral evidence; reported associations do not establish causal effects.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: IKEA Global Life at Home Report 2026 and Ingka Group release reviewed for quantitative sample, country weighting, home-needs importance and experience, optimism association, concerns, climate-action motivation, and age comparisons.
